title: What Really Happens During an Earthquake
description: Why earthquakes happen, how they are recorded and why they cannot be predicted, from the USGS and NASA.
narration: What actually happens when the ground shakes? Earth's outer shell is broken into giant puzzle pieces called tectonic plates. The plates keep slowly sliding past and bumping into each other. Rough edges snag on each other, so a fault locks in place even as the plates around it keep creeping along. While the fault stays locked, energy keeps being stored up. When the force finally beats the friction, the fault unsticks and all that energy is released as seismic waves, like ripples on a pond. Instruments called seismographs record the shaking. Scientists have tried many ways to predict earthquakes, but no method has worked, and they cannot say when the next one will strike on any fault.
